    Problem solved? New Volkswagen ID. Tiguan aims to fix the ID.4's weaknesses

    By Ted Welford
    Published: 09 October 2026
    Follow Car on Google
    Add Car as a preferred source on Google to see more of our latest content
    View all Volkswagen Reviews
    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 6:00
    Instaread

    ► ID.4 gets a new name as part of big facelift
    ► More user-friendly interior with lots more buttons
    ► And some lashings of VW retro

    Volkswagen has revealed the new ID. Tiguan, the new name for the ID.4, that aims to address that car’s criticisms with a redesigned interior and chunkier styling. 

    Replacing both the ID.4 and ID.5, the new ID. Tiguan has a completely redesigned interior with lots of new buttons to the interior and improving the quality. The firm is calling it a ‘True Volkswagen’, with similar changes being pulled off effectively on the ID. Polo, it’s now time for VW’s EV best-seller to get the same treatment.

    powered by

    Why the new name?

    Bluntly, because Tiguans sell and ID.4s don’t. That might be a harsh way to look at it given the ID.4 has been far from a sales flop, but with the Tiguan being Volkswagen’s most popular car worldwide, and being a similar size to the ID.4, it’s a no-brainer. It’s worth noting that it shares next to nothing in common with the petrol/diesel/hybrid Tiguan, which will continue for many years to come. 

    We’ve seen the same recently with the ID. Polo (originally due to be called ID.2) and the next ID.3 will get the Golf name, too. It’s all part of Volkswagen looking back on its heritage as a way to set it apart from Chinese competition. 

    Tell me about the new look

    The ID. Tiguan looks quite a bit different to the ID.4, introducing Volkswagen’s latest design language and generally looks a bit chunkier and boxier – and more like an SUV – in profile than the more rounded ID.4. 

    At both the front and rear there are light bars that run across the width of the car with an illuminated Volkswagen badge in the centre, depending on version. The rear lights have a new 3D look and appear to float within the light bar – VW’s nicknamed them ‘whiskey glasses’.  Aerodynamics have been improved by new ‘air curtains’ at either side of the bumper to optimise airflow around the body and help to improve the electric driving range. 

    Another key characteristic is a new horizontal line that runs below the window line from the front to rear of the car. Volkswagen says it can be traced back to the first Golf and that it will be used on every new Volkswagen going forward. Proper door handles are back, too!

    LOOK AT ALL THOSE BUTTONS

    ‘We listened and we addressed criticism’ is Volkswagen’s main point with the ID. Tiguan, as it aims to sort out the compromised usability with lots and lots of proper switchgear with a more simplistic approach. 

    Like the ID. Polo and facelifted ID.3 Neo, it gets a strip of climate controls below the main touchscreen and no more silly capacitive buttons on the steering wheel. There are four electric window switch buttons now as well (instead of the two and a ‘rear’ button on the ID.4), all of which makes the ID. Tiguan a considerably easier car to interact with. 

    The front of the interior has also been redesigned with it being one of the first cars with Magsafe wireless smartphone chargers and a larger centre console armrest with additional storage beneath. 

    Though the fundamental packaging of the ID. Tiguan remains the same as the ID.4 previously, there is now a small frunk under the bonnet, allowing space for charging cables to be kept out of the way. 

    But there’s still lots of technology – and an optional passenger screen

    Despite the move to more physical buttons, there’s still plenty of the interior taken up by screens. The main 15-inch touchscreen is running new software and is much easier to use, while the digital instrument cluster is far larger than before. 

    Another new addition is a front passenger touchscreen, a first for a Volkswagen in Europe. It will be optional and runs a simpler setup than other cars with such feature – meaning it’s tinted and only visible from the passenger seat.

    Its dials can replicate the backlit displays of a Mk4 Golf

    As seen on the ID. Polo and ID.3 Neo, Volkswagen is playing the heritage card with its new generation of EVs, and this SUV is no different. Though the Tiguan name doesn’t have as much heritage as other VWs, it’s no less important. 

    There’s a dedicated ‘retro’ setting that changes the instrument cluster to look like the blue lacklit dials of the Golf Mk4. The main infotainment system can also be revised to show a more classic look of VW’s past icons, such as a Golf Mk1, Mk2 and Mk4, as well as a first-generation Tiguan and original Beetle. 

    It’s the first electric R-Line

    Another change for the ID. Tiguan is that it’s the first electric Volkswagen to be available in a sportier-looking R-Line trim. It’s a popular choice on the rest of its passenger car range but only now offered on an EV. 

    Specific bumpers give the R-Line a sportier appearance, with a larger air intake and more gloss black finishes instead of the usual unpainted plastic areas. The R-Line also comes with larger and specific 20-inch alloy wheels, along with vertical LED daytime running lights at the front. 

    What powertrains are available?

    Volkswagen will continue with the same powertrains as before with the ID. Tiguan, with the exception of the sportier GTX model, which has been dropped. 

    These include a 58kWh battery paired to a 187bhp rear electric motor or a 77kWh battery available with a 282bhp rear motor or 295bhp 4Motion with an additional front motor. Maximum claimed ranges have increased by around 20 miles thanks to efficiency improvements, giving a maximum claimed range of 372 miles for the 77kWh car and 280 miles for the smaller 58kWh battery. 

    The ID. Tiguan will go on sale in early 2027, with prices likely to carry on from around the current ID.4’s starting price of £37,000.
